method: Every over-proposed (false-positive vs. the ISMP gold standard) pick was manually reviewed, since the gold standard is not exhaustive -- a pick can be a real, defensible name-confusion risk without being in P_us.csv. Each pick was categorized as: 'same_product' (brand/generic name or same-product-line variant of the exact same drug -- not a distinct-drug confusion at all), 'plausible' (a real-world-defensible orthographic/phonetic near-miss the gold standard simply doesn't list), or 'spurious' (a genuine mismatch -- counts as a real precision error).

counts.note: 45 = 5 + 29 + 11 (fixed 2026-09-09: an earlier draft of this file was missing the 'humulin r u 100 -> humulin' item, so 'items' below had 44 entries; corrected to 45).

precision.note: recommended_adjusted = 52 / (52 + 5 same_product + 11 spurious) -- only the 29 'plausible' picks are excluded from the error count, since those are defensible from pure orthographic/phonetic pattern-matching plus the stated rules alone. 'same_product' picks (e.g. rituximab/rituxan) still count as errors: recognizing that two names refer to the same drug requires outside pharmacological/regulatory knowledge (brand-generic equivalence) that the model is never given or asked to reason about anywhere in the prompt, so it can't fairly be credited for 'knowing better'. alternate_excluding_same_product_too (0.825) is the more generous version if you DO want to give that benefit of the doubt.
